title: Unit – 2 : Session – 2 : SLO – 2 | Operational Concepts
sections: Section A – Match the Following (Answers)
1. PC (Program Counter) → C. Points to the next instruction to be executed
2. MAR (Memory Address Register) → D. Holds address for accessing memory
3. MDR (Memory Data Register) → E. Holds the fetched data or instruction
4. ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) → A. Performs arithmetic and logic operations
5. IR (Instruction Register) → B. Temporarily holds instruction fetched from memory
Section B – Fill in the Blanks
At the start of execution, the PC (PROGRAM COUNTER) is set to point to the first instruction.
The address from the PC is loaded into the MAR, which initiates a read operation.
The fetched instruction is placed into the IR for decoding.
The ALU performs the operation, and the result is written back using the MAR and MDR.
An INTERRUPT is a service request by an I/O device to the processor.
Section C – Activity Task: Program Execution Cycle
1. Program load via input device: the program and its data are transferred from an input device into main memory.
2. Fetch cycle (PC → MAR → Memory → MDR → IR): PC sends the instruction address to MAR; memory is read; the instruction travels through MDR into IR.
3. Decode instruction: the Control Unit examines IR, identifies the operation and the operands needed.
4. Fetch operands: operand addresses are sent to MAR and the data is read into MDR/registers.
5. ALU execution: the ALU performs the required arithmetic or logic operation on the operands.
6. Write back result: the result is sent through MDR to memory or into a destination register.
7. PC increment: PC is updated to point to the next instruction and the cycle repeats.
Section D – True or False
The PC is used to perform arithmetic operations. — FALSE
The Instruction Register (IR) holds the address of data. — FALSE (it holds the instruction itself)
Interrupts help the processor handle I/O device requests. — TRUE
ALU operations are performed before fetching the instruction. — FALSE
After an interrupt is serviced, the processor resumes the program from where it was interrupted. — TRUE
